subject: SLA baseline & monthly credit timing — FinBridge request
messages:
From: Elena Suarez <elena@finbridge.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finbridge.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLA baseline, latency target, and monthly credit timing

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call this morning. Procurement asked me to follow up with our formal SLA asks so we can get this into our legal review. High level:

- Baseline uptime: 99.95% (monthly) across the US region.
- Latency: P95 under 200ms for text-generation endpoints (hosted API).
- Remedy: monthly service credit applied to the subsequent invoice within 30 days after the month close.
- Cap: credits should not exceed 25% of the monthly invoice for that bill cycle.
- Maintenance: scheduled maintenance windows should be excluded, but only if Redwood provides at least 72 hours notice; we want a maximum of 6 hours/month for scheduled maintenance to be excluded.
- Reporting: a monthly incident summary and one designated escalation contact.

Please confirm whether Redwood can accept these baseline numbers or point to the specific clauses you would want to align differently. For context, our renewal window is end of January, and procurement needs to see the SLA redline by Dec 15 to stay on schedule.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if you prefer.

Best,
Elena Suarez
Director, Procurement | FinBridge
elena@finbridge.com

Attachment: FinBridge_SLA_Request_20261125.pdf (PDF stub, 42 KB)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Elena Suarez <elena@finbridge.com>
Cc: procurement@finbridge.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA baseline, latency target, and monthly credit timing

Hi Elena — really appreciate the clear ask and the timeline. Quick response while we pull internal folks in:

- Uptime baseline: Redwood’s standard hosted SLA for comparable accounts is 99.90% monthly. We can consider a higher baseline for committed contracts / reserved capacity, but for hosted tier we typically cap at 99.90.
- Latency: P95 200ms is aggressive for mixed workloads. We can commit to P95 250ms for text-generation on our standard hosted nodes and propose a regional routing clause to prioritize lower-latency pools for production traffic. For burst / long-seq workloads we may include carveouts (we’ll flag this in the redline).
- Remedy & cap: We can apply service credits against the next invoice (invoice credit). Our finance prefers invoice-credit application rather than cash refunds. Standard cap we negotiate is 20% of monthly invoice; we can discuss moving toward 25% if we have committed reserved capacity or a longer-term term commitment.
- Maintenance: We generally provide 48–72 hours notice for planned maintenance and a typical monthly carveout target of up to 8 hours for rolling infra updates. We can tighten that to 6 hours/month with a maintenance blackout for peak regional windows if needed.
- Reporting & escalation: happy to provide monthly incident summaries and designate an escalation lead.

I’m looping in our legal/ops and finance partners to produce a clean redline consistent with your Dec 15 timeline.

Next steps from my side: internal alignment, finalize a counterproposal, and send a redline by Nov 29 for your review.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cell: 415-555-0182

(Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Summary.xlsx — short workbook with baseline metrics and regional routing options)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA baseline, latency target, and monthly credit timing (internal)

Jasmine — quick internal thoughts / suggested counterpoints to include in the Nov 29 redline: 

1) Baseline: Accept 99.90% for hosted. If FinBridge needs 99.95, we should condition that on either (a) reserved capacity (Dedicated) or (b) a 12+ month committed term with a minimum spend tier. That gives us capacity planning runway.

2) Latency: Offer P95 250ms for production-tagged routes in US-East/US-West (regional routing). Call out exceptions for batched inference and sequences >1024 tokens — these should be excluded from the P95 SLA or be measured separately.

3) Remedy timing: Finance prefers invoice credits applied to the next invoice cycle. We should retain a clause that allows Redwood to investigate and validate incidents before crediting. Add a 30-day dispute window for incidents.

4) Cap: Propose a sliding cap model: default cap 20% monthly; if FinBridge commits to reserved capacity we will increase cap to 25%. This is a helpful commercial lever.

5) Maintenance carveouts: Offer scheduled maintenance carveouts with 48 hours notice for minor infra work; require 72 hours for customer-impacting changes. Keep an allowance of up to 8 hours/month but propose an operational commitment to avoid peak hours for FinBridge’s primary traffic window (provide us the traffic window and we’ll lock a regional blackout).

6) Credit application mechanics: Recommend credits apply as an invoice offset and spell out timing (appear on next invoice within the following billing cycle). Also call out an annual cap on cumulative credits across the account (e.g., not to exceed 6 months of average monthly credits aggregated) — optional.

Ben — finance impact? If we invoice-credit (not cash) we minimize cashflow risk; if procurement insists on cash refunds that will escalate to revenue ops.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com; jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Subject: Re: SLA baseline & credits (finance view)

Jasmine / Laura — my two cents:
- Invoice-credit only. No cash refunds.
- Laddered remedy schedule (example):
  * >= 99.90%: no credit
  * 99.50% – 99.89%: 5% monthly invoice credit
  * 99.00% – 99.49%: 15% monthly invoice credit
  * < 99.00%: 25% monthly invoice credit (cap)
- Timing: Credits applied on next invoice; if incident dispute raised we have 30 days to investigate before final credit is applied.
- Reporting: require a single consolidated incident report each month.

If procurement pushes for 25% cap unconditionally, we should ask for longer term commitment or a higher committed spend.

—Ben
(finance)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Elena Suarez <elena@finbridge.com>
Cc: procurement@finbridge.com; Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>; Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Final counterproposal & redline delivery — SLA baseline and credit mechanics

Hi Elena — thanks for the patience. Per our internal alignment please find Redwood’s counterproposal below and the attached redline for your legal team. High-level summary:

- Uptime baseline (hosted): 99.90% monthly. If FinBridge moves to a Reserved (Dedicated) tier or commits to a 12-month minimum spend (TBD in the SOW) we will re-evaluate and can accept 99.95%.
- Latency: P95 target 250ms for production-tagged routes in US-East/US-West. Exclude batched inference and sequences >1024 tokens from this measurement (we list exact measurement endpoints in the redline).
- Remedy ladder (monthly invoice credits):
  * >= 99.90%: no credit
  * 99.50%–99.89%: 5% credit
  * 99.00%–99.49%: 15% credit
  * < 99.00%: 25% credit (cap)
- Credit cap & timing: Default monthly cap 20% (applies to hosted accounts). If FinBridge commits to Reserved capacity or a 12-month term, cap increases to 25% for the duration of that commitment. Credits will be applied as invoice offsets on the next billing cycle after validation, subject to a 30-day incident validation window.
- Maintenance carveouts: Scheduled maintenance excluded with 72 hours notice for customer-impacting changes; up to 8 hours/month allowance. We will work with you to define a regional blackout for FinBridge’s peak window.
- Reporting & escalation: Redwood will provide a consolidated monthly incident summary and name a single escalation lead (Ops: ops-esc@redwood.com).

Attached: Redwood_SLA_Counter_v1.docx (redline of the SLA with measurement language, remedies, and carveouts). Also attached is a short workbook with metrics mapping and examples.

If this aligns, we can circulate a version for DocuSign and schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal call next week to close redlines. If FinBridge still requires baseline 99.95 for hosted without commitment, we’ll need to price-match that into the commercial SOW (we can provide a committed-reserved-capacity quote).

Would you like us to prepare a clean contract with the Reserved capacity option and a pro forma pricing sheet, or proceed with hosted redline + 12-month term conversation?

Best,
Jasmine Liu
